newsitem.title: UK: BT cuts price of calls to mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: BT cuts price of calls to mobile phones.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Wednesday it was cutting the price of calls from its fixed line network to the mobile networks of market leader Vodafone Group Plc and BT's majority-owned Cellnet company from August 7.

Reflecting lower payments agreed by BT and the two mobile telephone companies, BT said the price of daytime calls would be reduced by one pence to 36.5p per minute, the price of evening and night time calls would be cut by three pence to 22p per minute and weekend calls would come down by two pence to 10.5p per minute.
Calls are charged by the second, with a minimun charge of five pence, the company noted in a statement.

Payments to the other mobile operators, the two digital networks owned by Orange Plc and One2One are cheaper to call from BT telephones, but those charges will also continue to be reduced, BT said. It gave no details.
"We look forward to more reductions in the coming months," Keith Carrington, BT's pricing manager, said in a statement.
The price of calling a mobile telephone from a fixed line has prompted the telecommunications regulator Oftel to call for significant price cuts.
Oftel welcomed the price cuts but said they had further to fall. "It looks as if prices are still too high," an Oftel spokeswoman said.
Oftel director general Don Cruickshank has mainly blamed mobile telephone companies for charging too much for delivering calls to customers on their networks.
Oftel, which has called for mobile firms to negotiate lower interconnection charges with each other, is still investigating the matter and said it would be making a statement in due course.
